# Research: Login Page (001-login-page)

**Generated by**: `/speckit.plan`
**Date**: 2026-05-04
**Resolved unknowns**: 6 of 6 — all NEEDS CLARIFICATION items closed

---

## 1. Supabase SSR Package for Next.js App Router

**Decision**: Use `@supabase/ssr` + `@supabase/supabase-js`. Do NOT use `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs`.

**Rationale**: `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` is officially deprecated with no new features.
`@supabase/ssr` is the sole recommended SSR package for Next.js 13+ App Router projects.

**Alternatives considered**: `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` — deprecated, migration guide
points entirely to `@supabase/ssr`.

**Key versions**:
```
@supabase/supabase-js  ^2.x
@supabase/ssr          ^0.10.x (actual installed version)
```

**Environment variables** (new format — legacy `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` still works but will be deprecated):
```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://<project>.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_...
```

**Client creation pattern**:
- Browser (Client Components): `createBrowserClient()` from `@supabase/ssr`
- Server (Server Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers): `createServerClient()` from `@supabase/ssr` with Next.js `cookies()` store
- Middleware: `createServerClient()` built from `request.cookies` / `response.cookies`

---

## 2. Route Protection in Next.js Middleware

**Decision**: Place all session refresh + route guard logic in `middleware.ts` using
`createServerClient()` + `supabase.auth.getClaims()` (NOT `getSession()`).

**Rationale**: `getSession()` reads cookie values without re-validating the JWT signature — it
can be spoofed. `getClaims()` validates the JWT against Supabase's published public keys on
every call, making it safe for server-side authorization decisions.

**Alternatives considered**: Protecting routes in layouts only — insufficient, because Next.js
App Router layouts don't re-render on every client-side navigation.

**Pattern**: `middleware.ts` at the project root calls an `updateSession()` helper that:
1. Creates a `createServerClient` instance wired to `request.cookies` and `supabaseResponse.cookies`
2. Calls `supabase.auth.getClaims()` to validate the session
3. Redirects unauthenticated requests (not `/login`, not `/auth/*`) to `/login`
4. Returns `supabaseResponse` (including any `Set-Cookie` headers for token refresh) unchanged

---

## 3. Open Redirect Prevention for `next` Parameter

**Decision**: Validate the `next` parameter: allow only values that start with `/` but NOT `//`.
Fall back to `/` for all other values.

**Rationale**: Attackers pass absolute URLs (`https://evil.com`) or protocol-relative URLs
(`//evil.com`). A `startsWith('/')` check alone passes `//evil.com`. The double-check
(`startsWith('/') && !startsWith('//')`) closes this.

**Alternatives considered**: Allowlist of exact paths — too rigid. Protocol blocklist regex —
fragile and harder to audit.

**Safe redirect helper**:
```ts
function getSafeRedirect(next: string | null, fallback = '/'): string {
  if (!next) return fallback
  if (next.startsWith('/') && !next.startsWith('//')) return next
  return fallback
}
```

---

## 4. App Router Folder Structure for Auth Pages

**Decision**: Route group `app/(auth)/` for auth pages with a shared unauthenticated layout.
OAuth/email route handlers live at `app/auth/` (outside the group) so their URLs are `/auth/callback`
and `/auth/confirm` — matching the URLs registered in the Supabase dashboard.

**Rationale**: Route groups (`(auth)`) apply a shared layout without adding a URL segment. The
Supabase dashboard Redirect URL must exactly match `/auth/callback`; placing it inside a route
group does not change the URL but could cause confusion.

**Alternatives considered**: Flat structure (`app/login/page.tsx`) — simpler but no shared
layout support.

**Final structure**:
```
app/
  (auth)/
    layout.tsx          ← centered card layout, no navigation, with app branding
    login/
      page.tsx          ← Google sign-in page (Server Component)
      actions.ts        ← signInWithOAuthAction('google') Server Action
  auth/
    callback/
      route.ts          ← OAuth PKCE code exchange (cookies written onto redirect response)
  (protected)/
    layout.tsx          ← authenticated shell, redirects unauthenticated to /login
    page.tsx            ← dashboard (redirect destination after login)
```

> **Descoped**: `register/`, `forgot-password/`, and `auth/confirm/` were planned but removed
> (Supabase free-tier email limit). `middleware.ts` is `proxy.ts` in Next.js 16; the export
> is named `proxy`, not `middleware`.

---

## 5. OAuth Callback Route (PKCE Code Exchange)

**Decision**: `app/auth/callback/route.ts` — GET handler that calls
`supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code)`, then redirects to a sanitized `next` param.

**Rationale**: Supabase SSR uses PKCE flow. The authorization server sends `?code=` to the
callback URL. The code verifier is stored in a cookie during the initial redirect. The route
handler must exchange the code server-side to write session tokens back to cookies.

**Alternatives considered**: Client-side implicit flow — Supabase SSR does not use implicit
flow. PKCE is required for secure server-side token exchange.

**Production origin handling**: Use `x-forwarded-host` header to construct the correct base
URL when behind a reverse proxy / Vercel edge network.

---

## 6. Form Validation Strategy [DESCOPED]

**Status**: Not applicable. Registration was descoped; the login page has no form fields.
Google OAuth is the only authentication method — no client-side or server-side field
validation is required. `zod` and `react-hook-form` remain installed but are unused.

> Original rationale (for reference): React Hook Form + Zod was chosen for real-time
> confirm-password cross-field feedback on the registration form. Server-side re-validation
> with the same Zod schema would have prevented bypass via direct POST requests.

**Packages**:
```
react-hook-form       ^7.x
@hookform/resolvers   ^3.x
zod                   ^3.x
```
